subject: Environment division structure
notes: Rule §12.2.1: 'ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.' (both words underlined, period required) followed by '[ configuration-section ]' then '[ input-output-section ]' -- both optional, in that order. Grammar environmentDivision = ENVIRONMENT DIVISION DOT configurationSection? inputOutputSection? matches exactly (no binder/validation pass narrows it; ClosedFormatPass line 132 only names the node). Probed with pinned cobol.exe at --std 85/2002/2014/2023: empty division, CONFIGURATION only, INPUT-OUTPUT only, both in order, empty section headers alone -> all compile and run correctly; INPUT-OUTPUT before CONFIGURATION -> COBOL0001 unexpected 'CONFIGURATION' (correct rejection, order is fixed by the format); header without period -> COBOL0307 (correct). cite.py --check 12.2.1 '[ configuration-section ]' -> OK; '[ input-output-section ]' -> OK. No spec-derived test targets this format (order rejection has no negative golden) -> test-ref empty = test-needed. Probes: out/probe/env-div/{A,B,C,D,E,G,H,N}.cob. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the §12.2.1 format carries no edition gating; unchanged across editions)] retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.cs#EnvDivisions (kb/Work PB3154 deleted DataBinder.EnvDivisions: a unit now carries at most one environment division (an OO definition's synthetic unit only its own; a class definition's configuration reaches its factory and instance definitions by InheritConfiguration), so BindDeclarations reads its configuration section and BindFileControl its input-output section through the singular environmentDivision() accessor)
